module_title: MS Word - Foundational Basics and Core Interface
introduction: In the 'Computer Knowledge' section of SSC CGL and Banking exams, MS Word is arguably the highest-weightage topic. It is a 'Word Processing' software used to create documents, letters, and reports. At this level, we focus on the basic interface, default settings, and universal keyboard shortcuts.

core_concepts.title: Default Settings (Highly Tested)
core_concepts.description: When you open a new MS Word file (2007 or newer), the default file name is 'Document1'. The default font face is 'Calibri' and the default font size is '11 pt'.

core_concepts.title: What is the Ribbon?
core_concepts.description: The Ribbon is the wide band across the top of the Word window that contains all the commands, grouped into Tabs (like Home, Insert, Layout). You can hide or show (collapse/expand) the ribbon instantly using the shortcut `Ctrl + F1`.

core_concepts.title: Basic Formatting Shortcuts
core_concepts.description:
Formatting is the process of changing the appearance of text. 
- Bold: `Ctrl + B`
- Italic: `Ctrl + I`
- Underline: `Ctrl + U`
- Undo (cancel the last action): `Ctrl + Z`
- Redo (repeat the canceled action): `Ctrl + Y`

core_concepts.title: Title Bar & Status Bar
core_concepts.description:
- Title Bar: The topmost bar of the window that displays the name of the file (e.g., Document1).
- Status Bar: The bottom-most bar that displays the current Page Number, Word Count, and contains the Zoom Slider.

important_entities.name: File Extension
important_entities.significance: Up to Word 2003, the file extension was `.doc`. From Word 2007 onwards, the default extension was updated to `.docx` (the 'x' stands for XML, making files lighter and safer).

important_entities.name: Zoom Percentage
important_entities.significance: In MS Word, the minimum zoom level is 10%, and the maximum zoom level is 500%. (Note: In MS Excel, the max zoom is only 400%).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A very common beginner trap! A file created in MS Word is strictly called a 'Document'. Never refer to it as a 'Spreadsheet' or 'Workbook' (which belong to Excel) or a 'Presentation' (which belongs to PowerPoint).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Remember the three most used clipboard commands sit right next to each other on the bottom row of the keyboard: `Ctrl + X` (Cut), `Ctrl + C` (Copy), and `Ctrl + V` (Paste).

exam_strategy_tips: SSC Tier-1 exams frequently ask for direct shortcuts. Always lock in the basic formatting keys. Also, remember that 'Calibri 11' is the modern standard default, replacing the old 'Times New Roman 12' used before 2007.
